categories.main_business_segments: United Rentals operates two primary business segments: General Rentals and Specialty. The General Rentals segment focuses on the rental of construction, aerial, and industrial equipment, general tools, and light equipment, serving a broad range of customers. The Specialty segment provides trench safety, power and HVAC, fluid solutions, mobile storage, modular office space, and surface protection mats, with a focus on infrastructure, industrial, and municipal customers.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages a proprietary software platform, Total Control®, to provide customers with real-time equipment management and digital rental services. Operations are supported by advanced information technology systems for fleet management, logistics, and customer service, as well as Lean management techniques and kaizen processes to drive operational efficiency and continuous improvement in equipment preparation, delivery, and maintenance.
categories.primary_customers_markets: United Rentals serves a highly diversified customer base, including large construction and industrial companies, manufacturers, utilities, municipalities, and homeowners. Its principal end-markets are industrial and non-construction (49% of rental revenue), commercial construction (46%), and residential construction (5%), with a strong focus on large key accounts and national accounts.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company primarily operates in the United States and Canada, with a smaller but growing presence in Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. As of January 2025, United Rentals had 1,686 rental locations, including 1,433 in the U.S., 158 in Canada, 39 in Europe, and 56 in Australasia.
categories.supply_chain_position: United Rentals operates downstream in the supply chain as an equipment rental and services provider, acting as an intermediary between equipment manufacturers and end users in construction, industrial, and municipal sectors. The company also sells new and used equipment and contractor supplies, and provides repair and maintenance services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic priorities include expanding its core equipment rental business through organic growth and acquisitions, optimizing customer and fleet mix, enhancing digital and technology offerings (notably Total Control®), and driving operational efficiencies via Lean management. United Rentals is also focused on expanding specialty offerings, cross-selling, and sustainability initiatives, including greenhouse gas intensity reduction and providing low- and zero-emissions equipment.
categories.revenue_model: United Rentals generates revenue primarily through equipment rentals (85% of total revenue in 2024), supplemented by sales of used and new equipment, contractor supplies, and service/other revenues. Rental contracts are typically short-term (hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly), and ancillary fees such as delivery, pickup, fuel, and damage waivers are significant contributors.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company is the largest equipment rental provider in the world, holding approximately 15% market share in North America. Its competitors include small independent businesses, regional players, national and global companies, and equipment dealers who both sell and rent equipment. United Rentals differentiates itself through scale, purchasing power, fleet diversity, and technology-enabled service.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, United Rentals reported total revenues of $15.3 billion, net income of $2.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA of $7.2 billion. The company has demonstrated steady growth, with an 8% increase in equipment rental revenue year-over-year and ongoing expansion through acquisitions (e.g., Yak Access in 2024 and the pending H&E acquisition). The company maintains significant liquidity and a large asset base, with $21.4 billion in fleet OEC.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: United Rentals emphasizes its ability to serve as a one-stop shop for jobsite solutions, offering the largest and most diverse rental fleet, extensive geographic reach, and advanced digital tools like Total Control® for customer equipment management. Its scale enables superior service, rapid equipment availability, competitive pricing, and strong national account support, while its specialty offerings and technology integration further differentiate it from competitors.
